references.text: This is the original account of the event to which the Levite refers, where the men of Gibeah surrounded the house and abused his concubine to death.
The verse describes how the men abused the concubine all night, leading to her death, which the Levite mentions in his testimony.
Here the Levite finds his concubine dead, confirming his statement that she died as a result of the abuse.
The Sodom incident has a similar motive, where men surround a house at night with evil intentions toward the guests.
The prophet Hosea refers to Gibeah as a place known for sin and wickedness, linking it to this event.
Hosea again mentions the days of Gibeah as an example of deep corruption in Israel.
Yet another reference to the sin of Gibeah as a turning point in Israel's history marked by evil.
